test_title: PYST 01: SSC Stenographer - English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 10 Dec 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given in indirect speech .

The customer asked the tailor, “Will you have the dress ready by Tuesday?”

options.text: The customer asked the tailor if he would have the dress ready by Tuesday.
The customer asked the tailor if he would like to have the dress ready by Tuesday
The customer asked the tailor if he will have the dress ready by Tuesday
The customer asked the tailor if he should have the dress ready by Tuesday

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The customer asked the tailor if he would have the dress ready by Tuesday.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Pronoun:**
 
 
• In direct speech, "you" is changed to "he" to align with the subject of the reporting verb.
 
 
 
• **Tense:**
 
 
• The modal verb "will" in direct speech is changed to "would" in indirect speech to follow the sequence of tenses rule.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "asked" indicates a question and requires the use of "if" to introduce the subordinate clause in indirect speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
 
• The sentence is restructured to integrate the question into a subordinate clause.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The customer asked the tailor if he would have the dress ready by Tuesday."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "The customer asked the tailor if he would like to have the dress ready by Tuesday." – Incorrect as it changes the original meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** "The customer asked the tailor if he will have the dress ready by Tuesday." – Incorrect tense (uses "will" instead of "would").
 
• **Option 4:** "The customer asked the tailor if he should have the dress ready by Tuesday." – Incorrect modal verb (changes the sentence’s meaning).
